title: Basis of SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme and Considerations for Applications
what_it_is: Basis of SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme and Considerations for Applications

sections.label: SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme questions
sections.summary: Questions asked on the scheme's design, assessment of conditions, appeals, and other financial assistance, plus three oral questions for 10 September 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what are the bases and considerations in the design of the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme; (b) how will the assessment be done as to whether individuals applying to the scheme meet the conditions required; and (c) whether there will be avenues for appeals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether recipients under the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme will benefit from other forms of short-term financial assistance from the Ministry of Social and Family Development or that provided at the constituency level.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In addition, I will address three oral questions scheduled for the Sitting tomorrow, 10 September 2024.

sections.label: Income criterion for scheme
sections.summary: The scheme targets lower- to middle-income workers earning up to $5,000 monthly before involuntary unemployment, benefiting over six in 10 such residents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To Ms Hazel Poa’s question, we have targeted the scheme at the lower- to-middle-income worker earning up to $5,000 per month before becoming involuntarily unemployed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: With this income criterion, more than six in 10 residents who are involuntarily unemployed can benefit from the scheme.

sections.label: Payout quantum and job search
sections.summary: Up to $6,000 over six months is paid to eligible applicants who have demonstrated active job search efforts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The payout quantum of up to $6,000 over six months is provided to eligible applicants who have demonstrated active job search efforts.

sections.label: Concurrent SkillsFuture Level-Up eligibility
sections.summary: Beneficiaries can concurrently qualify for the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme if they meet its eligibility criteria, and the scheme will be regularly reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Similarly to Mr Gan Thiam Poh's question, beneficiaries of the Jobseeker Support scheme can concurrently qualify for the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme that supports mid-career individuals to pursue substantive upskilling and reskilling, as long as they meet the eligibility criteria for all of these respective schemes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To conclude, Mr Speaker, Sir, the Jobseeker Support scheme marks a paradigm shift for the Government and it reflects our commitment that we will always help and provide resources for those who step up and want to do more for themselves.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This is a reset in the Government's policies and, just as importantly, a reset of Singaporeans' views and attitudes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We will regularly review the scheme to ensure that we provide necessary support to the involuntarily unemployed.

sections.label: Sizing targets lower- to middle-income
sections.summary: The scheme is targeted at the lower- to middle-income worker earning up to $5,000 per month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In our sizing of this scheme itself, we have targeted the scheme at the lower- to middle-income worker earning up to $5,000 per month.

sections.label: Property annual value threshold
sections.summary: Annual value of residential property is used as a wealth proxy, with a $25,000 threshold aligned with schemes like GST Voucher, covering about 75% of properties.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We also used the annual value of residential property as a proxy to determine households' wealth because this is, again, similar to other Government support schemes that provide higher benefits to individuals or households with lower means.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This threshold of $25,000 for the Jobseeker Support scheme is aligned with other schemes, such as the GST Voucher scheme, and it covers about 75% of residential properties, including all HDB flats.

sections.label: Appeals for private estate Singaporeans
sections.summary: The Government will consider individuals who do not meet eligibility criteria on a case-by-case basis, including appeals from Singaporeans in private estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the fact that we have to tightly control the criteria as we roll this landmark programme out, can the Government consider appeals for Singaporeans in private estates, with deserving circumstances, such as those living in households with a low per capita income – large households, I mean – those with limited housing equity and those who do not own the private housing that they live in?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I want to reassure the Member that we will consider individuals who do not meet the eligibility criteria on a case-by-case basis.

sections.label: Mature worker training and support payouts
sections.summary: A mature worker in the SkillsFuture Level-Up course can get up to $3,000 monthly training allowance and, if involuntarily unemployed, Jobseeker Support, potentially $21,000 over six months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For a mature worker who is now undergoing the SkillsFuture Level-Up course, the training allowance cap is up to $3,000 per month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: If he gets involuntarily unemployed, the Jobseeker Support scheme will be eligible for him.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, over that six-month horizon, he could, on top of getting up to $6,000 from the Jobseeker Support scheme, he could add on another $2,500 times six months, which is about $15,000 of the SkillsFuture Level-Up training allowance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And that comes up to an amount of up to, potentially, $21,000 over the six-month period.

sections.label: Scheme coverage up to median
sections.summary: Sizing the scheme up to slightly above median, the $5,000 mark, would benefit about six in 10 involuntarily unemployed workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We acknowledged the fact that the scheme does not cover everyone.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But for starters, when we sized this to go up to just slightly above median, that means up to the $5,000 mark, it would reach and it would benefit about six in 10 workers who are involuntarily unemployed.

sections.label: Scheme start and annual cost
sections.summary: The scheme will cost about $200 million a year to continue running.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, we want to make sure that the scheme gets off to a good footing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This will already cost us about $200 million a year to continue to run this.

sections.label: Scheme benefits and funding source
sections.summary: The scheme is expected to help more workers get back into good jobs faster and will be funded through the Government operating budget.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: With the scheme, we believe that an even higher proportion of workers will be able to benefit and get back into a good job faster.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: It will be funded through the Government operating budget.
